rules.statement: OS process limit (RLIMIT_NPROC/cgroup pids.max) exhaustion on the target host prevented new Oracle server process creation
causal_chain: OS process count for the oracle user approaches/reaches the configured limit
fork() fails for new Oracle server processes (ORA-27300/ORA-27301/ORA-27302)
new connections/sessions cannot be established
service disruption observed by clients

supporting_conditions.description: OS process count at/near the configured RLIMIT_NPROC/cgroup pids.max limit
fork() failures measured on the target host for the oracle user

contradicting_conditions.description: process count well below the configured limit contradicts exhaustion

temporal_proof_condition.description: fork() failures stopped exactly when the process limit was raised — unambiguous temporal proof

manual_actions.action_summary: Increase RLIMIT_NPROC / cgroup pids.max for the oracle OS user after capacity review
manual_actions.precheck: Confirm current process count, headroom and binding constraint via os/process-limits and os/cgroups
manual_actions.risk: OS-level configuration change, requires coordination with platform/infra team and service review
manual_actions.postcheck: Re-measure nproc_utilization_percent and fork_failures_observed after the change

rules.statement: A hung/unresponsive listener process caused inbound connection failures
causal_chain: listener process stops responding to new connection requests
clients receive ORA-12537/ORA-12170 on connect attempts
application-visible outage

supporting_conditions.description: listener process confirmed unresponsive to a local ping check
listener process thread count anomalous on the host

contradicting_conditions.description: listener process confirmed responsive contradicts a hang

manual_actions.action_summary: Restart the affected listener during an approved maintenance window
manual_actions.precheck: Confirm no active sessions will be dropped unexpectedly; notify affected application owners
manual_actions.risk: Brief connection interruption for new connections during restart
manual_actions.postcheck: Confirm listener responds to a local ping and accepts new connections

rules.statement: Storage-layer latency caused elevated db file sequential read wait times
causal_chain: underlying storage latency increases
single-block read I/O takes longer to complete
db file sequential read wait time increases
query/transaction response time degrades

supporting_conditions.description: db file sequential read average wait time elevated
I/O queue depth elevated on the underlying storage

contradicting_conditions.description: OS-level iostat shows normal I/O wait, contradicting a storage-latency cause
storage layer reports normal latency, contradicting a storage-latency cause

manual_actions.action_summary: Engage storage/infrastructure team to review underlying array/path health
manual_actions.precheck: Confirm affected LUNs/datastores and current queue depth
manual_actions.risk: None from this analysis step; any storage remediation is the infrastructure team's own change
manual_actions.postcheck: Re-measure db file sequential read average after storage-side remediation

rules.statement: TEMP tablespace saturation prevented temp segment extension
causal_chain: TEMP tablespace utilization reaches the configured critical threshold
a session requires additional temp segment space
ORA-01652 is raised, the operation fails

supporting_conditions.description: TEMP tablespace utilization at/above 95% at the time of the symptom
TEMP tablespace autoextend has reached its maximum size

contradicting_conditions.description: TEMP tablespace utilization well below saturation contradicts exhaustion

manual_actions.action_summary: Manually add/resize a TEMP tablespace datafile after capacity review
manual_actions.precheck: Confirm available disk headroom on the underlying filesystem/ASM diskgroup
manual_actions.risk: None from this analysis step; the resize itself is a manual DBA-executed change
manual_actions.postcheck: Re-measure tablespace_used_percent after the manual resize

rules.statement: RAC interconnect degradation (packet loss under an MTU mismatch) led to a node eviction
causal_chain: interconnect MTU mismatch between cluster nodes
interconnect packet loss/fragmentation increases
cluster communication (CSS heartbeat) degrades
node eviction is triggered
service disruption on the evicted node

supporting_conditions.description: interconnect MTU mismatch detected between cluster nodes

contradicting_conditions.description: interconnect packet loss negligible, contradicting a network-degradation cause

manual_actions.action_summary: Correct the interconnect MTU mismatch across all cluster nodes after a coordinated maintenance window
manual_actions.precheck: Confirm current MTU configuration on every interconnect interface across all nodes
manual_actions.risk: Requires a coordinated network configuration change across the cluster
manual_actions.postcheck: Re-measure interconnect_packet_loss_percent after the MTU correction

rules.statement: cgroup pids.max constraint (distinct from RLIMIT_NPROC) prevented new Oracle server process creation
causal_chain: cgroup pids.max for the oracle.slice unit approaches/reaches its configured limit
fork() fails for new Oracle server processes (ORA-27300/ORA-27301/ORA-27302)
new connections/sessions cannot be established
service disruption observed by clients

supporting_conditions.description: cgroup pids.max utilization at/near its configured limit

contradicting_conditions.description: cgroup pids.max utilization well below its limit contradicts this cause

manual_actions.action_summary: Increase the cgroup pids.max limit for the oracle.slice unit after capacity review
manual_actions.precheck: Confirm current cgroup pids.max utilization and binding constraint via os/cgroups
manual_actions.risk: OS-level configuration change, requires coordination with platform/infra team
